newsitem.title: CANADA: Spar sees possible Q3 break-even or profit.
newsitem.headline: Spar sees possible Q3 break-even or profit.

text.p: Space and communications equipment maker Spar Aerospace Ltd will inch closer to break-even or a profit in the third quarter, Chief Financial Officer Mark Steinman said on Tuesday.

"Next quarter it's going to be close," Steinman, newly promoted to acting chief executive at Spar's ComStream communications unit, told Reuters in a telephone interview. Depending on the results from money-losing ComStream, Spar could be profitable in the fourth quarter, he added. Spar said today it lost C$1.6 million or C$0.11 a share in the second quarter from continuing operations.
Because of ComStream's second-quarter losses, "we're a little behind where we'd like to be," Steinman said.
ComStream posted an operating loss of C$1.5 million in the second quarter versus a year earlier loss of C$6.2 million.
"The third quarter we're going to show numbers around the same for Comstream," Steinman said. "But in the fourth quarter we expect it (Comstream) to be profitable."
Steinman noted that the orders for the unit's satellite dish technology had taken too long to materialize and fill.
Spar, which is considering possible offers from companies to buy or merge with ComStream, would likely decide on the unit's future in the next three to six months, Steinman said.
Spar shares rose 0.05 to 9.45 today in light trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange, slightly above their 52-week low of 9.25. The stock's 52-week high is 16.30.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109 or lydia.zajc@reuters.com))
